title: SDK tool contract executor with schema fallback modes and cross-SDK examples
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: SDK users integrate Open-style tool/function calling but encounter frequent schema mismatches between model outputs and the declared function contract. Current SDK helpers enforce strict schema validation and drop streamed partial results, causing friction for streaming chat + tool workflows and brittle retry semantics across languages.

Goal: Provide a cross-SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) "executor" helper that: (1) performs configurable schema validation (strict/lenient/coerce), (2) supports streaming invocation with resumable schema-tolerant checkpoints, (3) supplies idempotency and retry glue that works with streamed partial outputs, and (4) ships clear language-specific ergonomic examples and test harnesses. The feature should be opt-in behind a feature flag and accompanied by documentation, examples, and a rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a unified Executor API in Python/TypeScript/Go that can be configured with 'validation_mode' (strict, permissive, coerce)
Executor can run synchronous and streaming function/tool calls and returns a unified result object with metadata about validation errors and recovered fields
Streaming paths support checkpointing so long-running streams can be resumed after transient network failures without losing validated payload context
Retries implement idempotency tokens and a retry strategy that avoids double-execution for side-effecting tools (docs and default behavior)
Comprehensive unit tests (+fuzz) show permissive mode recovers from common schema drift cases (missing fields, extra fields, simple type coercion)

Examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go illustrating strict validation (fail-fast), permissive validation (record warnings + return payload), and coercion (attempt best-effort conversion) are included in the SDK repo
Feature behind 'executor_v2' feature flag with telemetry to measure adoption and failure modes
Design doc and security review completed and linked in ticket
tasks: Design: finalize validation modes and streaming resume protocol (Priya)
Design: draft API surface for Executor across SDKs and map idiomatic patterns for each language (Ethan)
Implementation: add Executor abstraction to python-sdk with validation plugin points (Engineer A)
Implementation: add Executor to ts-sdk with StreamAdapter and backpressure hooks (Engineer B)
Implementation: add Executor to go-sdk with lightweight interface and context-aware cancellation (Engineer C)
Testing: create fuzz test corpus simulating model-led schema drift and run across all SDKs
Docs: write examples and migration guide, add code samples to quickstart
Release: gate behind feature flag and add rollout dashboard to Console
comments: 2026-02-20 Priya Kapoor: Kicked off initial design exploration. Noticed two common failure modes: (1) model emits additional top-level keys (extra fields), (2) model omits optional nested arrays leading to runtime KeyError in consumer code. Proposed three modes: strict, permissive (collect warnings), coerce (try type conversions).

2026-02-24 Ethan Morales: Reviewed sketch. Concern about permissive mode leaking unexpected types into downstream systems. Suggest adding 'sanitizers' that are opt-in for side-effecting tools and a flag to require server-side confirmation before executing external actions.

2026-03-02 Priya Kapoor: Draft API: Executor.run(func_schema, input, validation_mode='permissive', idempotency_key=None, stream=False). Streaming returns async iterator (ts/python) and channel in go. Shared doc at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SDK-Executor-Design

2026-03-04 Engineer B: Implemented initial TS prototype: streaming adaptor with 'checkpoint' messages emitted every N validated function params; pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1423
2026-03-06 Security Review (notes): Need KMS usage for idempotency keys persisted in Dedicated/Private; ensure executor does not log full payloads by default. Security review requested: true

2026-03-08 QA: Found edge case where coercion of numeric strings to integers changed semantics for a payment-amount field. Decided coercion is disabled by default for fields matching label 'money' or 'currency' - sanitizer hook required for such conversions.

2026-03-10 Ethan Morales: Merging python prototype to staging branch after adding metrics. Added telemetry to track: validation_mode used, % messages auto-corrected in coerce, stream resume count, idempotent retry hits.
implementation_notes: Key decisions: (1) Keep validation extensible: validator plugins per-field with built-in rules for common types (uuid, iso-date, money); (2) Streaming: emit periodic 'checkpoint' envelope that records last validated index and KV cache pointers; (3) Retry semantics: default safe-retry uses idempotency key + deterministic executor checkpoint file; (4) Backwards compatibility: default validation_mode = 'permissive' to avoid breaking existing consumers; provide linter/warning during CI with 'strict' mode opt-in; (5) Language ergonomics: Python/TS provide async iterator wrappers; Go returns channel + ResumeToken struct.
testing_notes: Unit tests: positive/negative cases per validation_mode. Integration: end-to-end with model simulator that emits schema drift patterns. Fuzzing: generate mutated function outputs and assert no crash and correct diagnostics. Load test: streaming resume under transient network flaps. SDK interop test: validate that a streamed checkpoint from ts-sdk can be resumed by python-sdk using standard ResumeToken format.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood behind 'executor_v2' flag in staging (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta for select customers via support toggle and console switch (4 weeks). Phase 3: wider release and enable-by-default only after 2 weeks of zero critical incidents. Telemetry dashboard to measure validation failures, resume events, and retry dedupe rates.
